findings.evidence: The Statement assumes smoothness only in state and parameter variables but asserts local classical solutions without time regularity. F(t,x,lambda)=1 at t=0 and 0 otherwise satisfies that stated smoothness yet has no classical local solution through t0=0: derivative zero elsewhere forces constancy, contradicting derivative one at zero. The opened initial-data supplier assumes an existing common solution map. Wang, Banach Calculus, §§4.3–4.4, pp.13–16, preserves the C^p condition under augmentation and does not license this discontinuous-time case. Require joint smoothness or precise joint continuity hypotheses. The assigned consumer actually uses jointly smooth coefficients.
